title: Playing for Jesus and for the whole group, as his mother taught him
summary: His mother told him to dedicate his playing to Jesus and to speak of how the whole group played, which shaped his unhappiness when the band fell short.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, that he himself was having trouble. But George was a perfectionist in this playing. I mean, he was beautiful. When he played, he wanted to give himself completely. He got lost in this playing. Like I always used to say, whenever I thought of George Lewis's playing, or now for that matter, I would always tease him and I'd say, well, tonight you're going to go play with the angels again. Because to me, that's how he sounded, like he was talking to the angels when he played. Just talking with those angels. And he felt it because he said his mom always told him. She said, son, when you get up on that stage, when you're playing, don't ever say, I'm playing this for George Lewis. He says, I'm playing this for Jesus. Always say, I'm playing this for you, Jesus. And there was always that. He said, never once did he ever stop, did he ever get to play in front of the public, where he didn't say that to him, son. Or if he came back on tour, his mother always, she'd say, he'd come in the door and he would say, his mama would say, well, son, how did you make out? How did you all make out? And he says, oh, ma, I made out pretty good. She says, look, I didn't ask you, son, how you made out. She says, I asked you how you all made out. She says, because it didn't take just but you to play that group, to go overseas and play for the people. She said, it took the entire group. When you're speaking, she says, you're speaking of the group. And he said, they never forgot it. So when he spoke of his playing, he never spoke really. That's why he was so unhappy with the group if they didn't play up to his standard of what he wants to at all times, because he felt he himself wasn't playing. It was an entire group. It was just not singular. And he said, each man had to give of himself. They all contributed.
